# Happy

A voice assistant that operates your computer. Hold a key, say what you want, it happens.

Everything runs on your machine — the speech recognition, the model, the voice, the tools.
Nothing about a turn leaves the box unless you connect a service that is somewhere else.

```
  hold the key ─► record ─► transcribe ─► think ─► speak
      ears          ears        ears       brain    voice
                                             │
                                             ▼
                                      hands/ and eyes/
                                      (tools it calls)
```

## What it can do

Happy sees the screen and works the machine: opening apps, clicking and typing, reading files
whatever their format, changing sound and brightness and Wi-Fi, running a shell command,
searching the web. It remembers what you have said to it before.

It also reaches services that are not on this computer — mail, calendar, drive, Notion,
GitHub, Slack, the weather, WhatsApp — but only the ones you connect yourself, in the panel.
Nothing is connected out of the box.

## Install

macOS and Windows are both supported, always. One line:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/someone/happy/main/install.sh | sh
```

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/someone/happy/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

Everything it installs goes in one folder (`~/.happy`), and uninstalling is deleting it.
You need Python 3.11 or newer and git; the installer will tell you if either is missing.

To run from a clone instead:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/someone/happy.git
cd happy
./setup.sh          # setup.ps1 on Windows
python main.py
```

## Using it

Hold the trigger key, say the thing, let go. There is no wake word — holding a key is already
somebody saying who they are talking to, and it means the microphone is shut the rest of the
time, with the system's own microphone light off to prove it.

The menu bar icon opens a panel: what Happy heard, what it did, the settings, and the services
you can connect.

## How it is built

Every module is a folder named after the part of a person that does the job — `brain` thinks,
`ears` hear, `voice` speaks, `eyes` see, `hands` do, `memory` remembers, `face` shows. There is
exactly one model loop, in `brain/thinking.py`; the folders under `hands/` export tools and
think about nothing.

[HAPPY.md](HAPPY.md) is the full architecture: what each file owns, why the shape is what it
is, and the decisions that have already been made and unmade. Read it before changing anything
structural.

[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) is how code in this repo is written. Read it before writing any.

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). The short version: read `AGENTS.md`, keep files under
200 lines, and make it work on both macOS and Windows.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

"""Mouse control from hand state.

The index finger is a joystick. Where it rests becomes centre; tilt it off
centre and the cursor travels that way, bring it back and the cursor stops
where it is. Deflection is measured against the palm's own axes, so this is
finger movement, not hand movement -- rest your wrist and drive it with the
one finger. Hook the finger in to park and re-centre.

    fist             toggle control on / off
    index            steer -- swing it sideways, curl or straighten it
    hook the index   park, and drop the centre
    pinch 4-12       tap = left click, hold then tilt = drag
    pinch 4-16       right click
    pinch 4-20       hold and tilt up / down to scroll

The index does no clicking and the clicking fingers do no steering, so nothing
you do with a button can move the cursor.

Run:  .venv/bin/python controller.py     (q to quit, m to force control off)

macOS needs Accessibility permission for the app that launches python --
System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility. Without it the cursor
calls silently do nothing, so the script probes for it at startup.
"""

import math
import time

import cv2
import mediapipe as mp
from pynput.mouse import Button, Controller
from Quartz import CGDisplayBounds, CGMainDisplayID

import hand
from mappings import (
    DRAG_BREAKAWAY,
    DRAG_HOLD_S,
    DRAG_PINCH,
    DWELL_CLICK_S,
    DWELL_RADIUS_PX,
    FIST_COOLDOWN_S,
    FIST_HOLD_S,
    PINCH_BINDINGS,
    PINCH_ON,
    PINCH_REACH,
    SCROLL_MAX_LPS,
    SCROLL_PINCH,
    SCROLL_SIGN,
    STEER_CURVE,
    STEER_DEADZONE,
    STEER_EASE_S,
    STEER_FULL,
    STEER_MAX_SPEED,
    STEER_RECENTER_RATE,
    STEER_SUSPEND_MAX_S,
    STEER_TIP,
)


def can_control_mouse():
    """Probe whether macOS actually lets us move the cursor.

    Without an Accessibility grant pynput's position setter silently no-ops:
    the call succeeds and the event is dropped, so the app looks broken with
    no error at all. Nudge 1px, read back, restore.
    """
    mouse = Controller()
    start = mouse.position
    mouse.position = (start[0] + 1, start[1] + 1)
    time.sleep(0.05)
    moved = mouse.position != start
    mouse.position = start
    return moved


PERMISSION_HELP = """
Cannot move the cursor -- macOS Accessibility permission is missing.

Grant it to the app that LAUNCHES python, not to python itself:
    System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility

  VS Code terminal -> add "Visual Studio Code"
  Terminal.app     -> add "Terminal"

Then fully quit and reopen that app. Tracking still works; only the cursor
and click output are suppressed.
"""


def clamp(v, lo, hi):
    return lo if v < lo else hi if v > hi else v


PINCH_FINGERS = hand.pinch_fingers()   # action -> the finger that must reach


def why_not_moving(permitted, toggle_on, state, steering, stick):
    """One line saying exactly what is stopping the cursor, in the order the
    checks actually apply.

    A stalled cursor has one symptom and half a dozen causes -- no permission,
    control off, a hand that dropped out, a pinch holding the stick, or simply
    sitting inside the deadzone. Guessing between them from the outside is
    hopeless, so the program says which one it is and shows the number.
    """
    if not permitted:
        return "no Accessibility permission - see the note above", (0, 0, 255)
    if not toggle_on:
        return "control OFF - press space, or make a fist", (170, 170, 170)
    if state is None:
        return "no hand in frame", (0, 165, 255)
    if state["fist"]:
        return "fist held - release it to steer", (0, 165, 255)
    if not steering:
        held = state["pinch"] or state["closing_on"] or "a pinch"
        return f"stick held for {held}", (0, 200, 255)
    if stick.magnitude <= 0:
        return (f"centred - deflection {stick.deflection:.3f} of {STEER_DEADZONE:.2f} "
                f"needed", (150, 150, 150))
    return f"steering {int(stick.magnitude * 100)}%  {int(stick.speed())} px/s", (0, 255, 0)


class FistToggle:
    """Edge-triggered on/off switch driven by a sustained fist.

    A fist has to be *held* for FIST_HOLD_S before it flips anything, and the
    hand must open again before the next toggle -- otherwise one long fist
    would flap control on and off every frame. The cooldown stops a fist that
    relaxes and re-clenches from double-toggling.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.on = False
        self.fist_since = None
        self.armed = True          # must open the hand before toggling again
        self.last_toggle = None    # None, not 0.0 -- see the cooldown check below

    def update(self, is_fist, now):
        if not is_fist:
            self.fist_since = None
            self.armed = True
            return False

        if self.fist_since is None:
            self.fist_since = now

        held = now - self.fist_since
        # No previous toggle means no cooldown to serve. Comparing against 0.0
        # would gate the very first toggle on the absolute clock instead.
        cool_ok = self.last_toggle is None or (now - self.last_toggle) >= FIST_COOLDOWN_S

        if self.armed and held >= FIST_HOLD_S and cool_ok:
            self.on = not self.on
            self.armed = False
            self.last_toggle = now
            return True
        return False

    def hold_progress(self, now):
        """0..1 for the HUD bar, so you can see the toggle coming."""
        if self.fist_since is None or not self.armed:
            return 0.0
        return min((now - self.fist_since) / FIST_HOLD_S, 1.0)


class Stick:
    """The index finger as a self-centring joystick.

    Deflection from the captured centre commands a VELOCITY, not a position.
    That one change is what makes clicking work: at rest the commanded velocity
    is zero, so the cursor is not merely damped, it is genuinely stationary --
    and nothing the rest of the hand does can push it, because the rest of the
    hand is not in the loop.

    Deflection is read in the palm's frame (see hand.steer_vector), so it is
    the finger's ARTICULATION that steers, not the hand's position. You can
    rest your wrist on the desk and drive it with the one finger; sliding or
    turning the hand registers as nothing at all.

    It also removes the edges. There is no region of the frame that has to map
    onto the screen, so there is nowhere to run out of and no mapping to be off
    by. Hooking the finger drops the centre; straightening it captures a new
    one wherever you are.
    """

    def __init__(self, screen_w, screen_h, aspect):
        self.screen = (screen_w, screen_h)
        self.aspect = aspect          # frame h/w, so the two axes measure alike
        self.pos = (screen_w / 2.0, screen_h / 2.0)
        self.vel = (0.0, 0.0)
        self.center = None            # captured neutral, in palm-frame coords
        self.offset = (0.0, 0.0)      # deflection in palm widths, for the HUD
        self.deflection = 0.0         # its raw size, before the deadzone
        self.magnitude = 0.0          # deflection past the deadzone, 0..1
        self.active = False

    def park(self):
        """Stop and drop the centre: hand lost, index curled, or steering off."""
        self.vel = (0.0, 0.0)
        self.center = None
        self.offset = (0.0, 0.0)
        self.deflection = 0.0
        self.magnitude = 0.0
        self.active = False

    def _command(self, lm):
        """Deflection -> the velocity it asks for, in px/s.

        Always runs, even while steering is suspended. A suspended stick still
        has to KNOW it is being pushed: that push is what commits an armed
        pinch to a drag, and what turns the wheel while scrolling. Suspension
        only stops the velocity from being spent on the cursor.
        """
        v = hand.steer_vector(lm, self.aspect)

        if self.center is None:
            self.center = v

        # Swing stays sideways; reach is negated because straightening the
        # finger (reaching further from the knuckle) should send the cursor UP,
        # and screen y grows downward.
        dx = v[0] - self.center[0]
        dy = -(v[1] - self.center[1])
        self.offset = (dx, dy)

        # Normalize each axis against its own full-scale travel before taking
        # the magnitude, so a diagonal is a true diagonal even though the two
        # axes have very different amounts of finger movement available.
        nx = dx / STEER_FULL[0]
        ny = dy / STEER_FULL[1]
        dist = math.hypot(dx, dy)
        span = math.hypot(nx, ny)
        self.deflection = dist

        if dist <= STEER_DEADZONE:
            # At rest the centre creeps toward the finger, so the slow drift of
            # a resting hand never accumulates into a phantom deflection.
            self.magnitude = 0.0
            return (0.0, 0.0), True

        # Ramp from zero AT the deadzone edge rather than jumping to whatever
        # the raw deflection already was.
        dead = STEER_DEADZONE / max(dist, 1e-6) * span      # deadzone, in span units
        t = clamp((span - dead) / max(1.0 - dead, 1e-6), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.magnitude = t

        speed = (t ** STEER_CURVE) * STEER_MAX_SPEED
        scale = speed / max(span, 1e-6)
        return (nx * scale, ny * scale), False

    def update(self, lm, steering, dt, now):
        """`steering` is False while a pinch is closing, so the cursor is dead
        through the whole click -- press, hold and release."""
        self.active = steering
        command, resting = self._command(lm)

        if resting:
            # Only ever recentres inside the deadzone, so a deliberate push is
            # never eroded -- including one made while steering is suspended.
            v = hand.steer_vector(lm, self.aspect)
            k = min(STEER_RECENTER_RATE * dt, 1.0)
            self.center = (self.center[0] + (v[0] - self.center[0]) * k,
                           self.center[1] + (v[1] - self.center[1]) * k)

        target = command if steering else (0.0, 0.0)

        # Ease toward the commanded velocity so the cursor has a little mass.
        k = 1.0 if STEER_EASE_S <= 0 else min(dt / STEER_EASE_S, 1.0)
        self.vel = (self.vel[0] + (target[0] - self.vel[0]) * k,
                    self.vel[1] + (target[1] - self.vel[1]) * k)

        self.pos = (
            clamp(self.pos[0] + self.vel[0] * dt, 0, self.screen[0] - 1),
            clamp(self.pos[1] + self.vel[1] * dt, 0, self.screen[1] - 1),
        )
        return self.pos

    def speed(self):
        return math.hypot(*self.vel)


class MouseController:
    """Turns per-frame (pinch, stick) samples into mouse events.

    Left click resolves on release: a pinch that just started might still turn
    into a drag. Right click has its own finger and fires on contact, since
    there is nothing to disambiguate.
    """

    def __init__(self, screen_w, screen_h):
        self.mouse = Controller()
        self.screen = (screen_w, screen_h)

        self.pinch = None
        self.dragging = False        # armed: held long enough, no button yet
        self.drag_held = False       # committed: button is actually down
        self.start_time = 0.0
        self.scroll_accum = 0.0
        self.status = "idle"
        self.event = ""              # last discrete event, for the HUD
        self.event_at = 0.0
        self.suspend_armed = True
        self.suspend_since = None

        self.dwell_at = None
        self.dwell_since = None
        self.dwell_armed = True

    def steering_allowed(self, closing, now):
        """The stick is dead while a pinch forms, resolves, or scrolls.

        A committed drag is the exception -- it is movement by definition, so
        the stick comes back to life once the drag is real. Scrolling keeps the
        stick dead for the cursor and spends the deflection on the wheel
        instead, so scrolling cannot slide the cursor off the pane.

        The timeout is a backstop against a dead cursor. Suspension waiting for
        a click that never comes is indistinguishable, from the outside, from
        the app being broken -- so a wait that goes on too long gives movement
        back, and stays given back until the fingers open again.
        """
        if self.drag_held:
            return True
        if self.pinch is not None:
            self.suspend_armed = True     # a real pinch: suspend as long as it lasts
            self.suspend_since = None
            return False
        if not closing:
            self.suspend_armed = True
            self.suspend_since = None
            return True

        if not self.suspend_armed:
            return True
        if self.suspend_since is None:
            self.suspend_since = now
        elif (now - self.suspend_since) > STEER_SUSPEND_MAX_S:
            self.suspend_armed = False
            return True
        return False

    def _note(self, text, now):
        self.status = text
        self.event = text
        self.event_at = now

    def _down(self, action, now, live):
        self.start_time = now

        if action == DRAG_PINCH:
            self.status = "pinch..."
        elif action == SCROLL_PINCH:
            self.scroll_accum = 0.0
            self.status = "SCROLL"
        else:
            if live:
                self.mouse.click(Button.right, 1)
            self._note("RIGHT CLICK", now)

    def _up(self, action, now, live):
        self.dragging = False

        if self.drag_held:
            if live:
                self.mouse.release(Button.left)
            self.drag_held = False
            self._note("drop", now)
        elif action == DRAG_PINCH:
            # Nothing was ever pressed, so every left pinch that did not commit
            # to a drag ends here as a click -- however long you held it while
            # lining up. Two in quick succession land on the same pixel (the
            # stick was dead for both), so the OS reads a double click.
            if live:
                self.mouse.click(Button.left, 1)
            self._note("LEFT CLICK", now)
        else:
            self.status = "idle"

    def _scroll(self, stick, dt, live):
        """Rate-based, like the cursor: hold a deflection, the wheel keeps turning."""
        dy = stick.offset[1]
        if abs(dy) <= STEER_DEADZONE:
            return
        t = min((abs(dy) - STEER_DEADZONE) / max(STEER_FULL[1] - STEER_DEADZONE, 1e-6), 1.0)
        # offset y is already screen-sense (straighten = up), and pushing up
        # should scroll up, so the sign passes straight through.
        lines = math.copysign(t * SCROLL_MAX_LPS * dt, dy) * SCROLL_SIGN

        self.scroll_accum += lines
        ticks = int(self.scroll_accum)
        if ticks:
            self.scroll_accum -= ticks
            if live:
                # offset y is in screen sense (curl = down), pynput's wheel is
                # not: positive scrolls up.
                self.mouse.scroll(0, -ticks)

    def _dwell(self, pos, now, live):
        """Hover-to-click. Off unless DWELL_CLICK_S is set."""
        if self.dwell_at is None or math.dist(pos, self.dwell_at) > DWELL_RADIUS_PX:
            self.dwell_at = pos
            self.dwell_since = now
            self.dwell_armed = True
        elif self.dwell_armed and (now - self.dwell_since) >= DWELL_CLICK_S:
            if live:
                self.mouse.click(Button.left, 1)
            self.dwell_armed = False   # must leave the spot before it fires again
            self._note("DWELL CLICK", now)

    def update(self, pinch, stick, tracked, live, dt, now):
        """`live` is the fist toggle: when False we track and draw but emit nothing."""
        if pinch != self.pinch:
            if self.pinch is not None:
                self._up(self.pinch, now, live)
            if pinch is not None:
                self._down(pinch, now, live)
            self.pinch = pinch

        # Drag in two stages. Holding the pinch only ARMS it; the button goes
        # down when you then push the stick, which is unambiguous intent. A
        # hold that never pushes presses nothing, so it still ends as a click.
        if pinch == DRAG_PINCH and not self.dragging and not self.drag_held and \
                (now - self.start_time) >= DRAG_HOLD_S:
            self.dragging = True
            self.status = "drag armed - push to drag"

        # Commit on DEFLECTION, not on cursor travel: the cursor is held still
        # until the button is down, so waiting for it to move would deadlock --
        # it cannot move until it drags, and it cannot drag until it moves.
        # Pushing the stick is the intent; the press then lands on the pixel
        # you were sitting on, and movement starts from there.
        if self.dragging and not self.drag_held and stick.magnitude >= DRAG_BREAKAWAY:
            self.drag_held = True
            if live:
                self.mouse.press(Button.left)
            self._note("DRAG", now)

        if pinch == SCROLL_PINCH:
            self._scroll(stick, dt, live)

        if tracked and pinch is None and not self.drag_held and DWELL_CLICK_S > 0:
            self._dwell(stick.pos, now, live)
        else:
            self.dwell_at = None

        if live:
            self.mouse.position = stick.pos

    def release(self):
        """Never leave the button stuck down system-wide."""
        if self.drag_held:
            self.mouse.release(Button.left)
            self.drag_held = False
        self.dragging = False


def draw_stick(frame, lm, stick, steering, aspect):
    """Draw the joystick: centre, deadzone, and the current push.

    The centre lives in the palm's frame, so it is projected back into the
    image every frame -- it rides along as you move or turn your hand, which is
    exactly the point: it is pinned to your knuckle, not to the room.
    """
    h, w = frame.shape[:2]
    if stick.center is None:
        return

    cnorm = hand.steer_to_image(lm, stick.center, aspect)
    cx, cy = int(cnorm[0] * w), int(cnorm[1] * h)
    tip = lm[STEER_TIP]
    tx, ty = int(tip.x * w), int(tip.y * h)

    # Deadzone drawn at true size, so "how far past centre am I" is something
    # you can see rather than a number you have to translate.
    ring = int(STEER_DEADZONE * hand.palm_span_flat(lm, aspect) * w)

    live = steering and stick.magnitude > 0
    color = (0, 220, 255) if live else (120, 120, 120)
    cv2.circle(frame, (cx, cy), max(ring, 3), color, 2)
    cv2.circle(frame, (cx, cy), 3, color, -1)
    if live:
        cv2.arrowedLine(frame, (cx, cy), (tx, ty), (0, 220, 255), 3, tipLength=0.25)
